message.content:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) (as [a {field (that [has {become} central]) to} research]) has rapidly evolved from symbolic reasoning to data-driven systems. This introduction surveys the central problems—learning, representation, inference, and alignment—that define contemporary AI research. It first outlines the historical trajectory of the field, then examines key architectural advances, and finally considers open questions concerning interpretability, fairness, and societal impact. The goal is to frame AI not merely as a set of technical methods, but as an evolving interdisciplinary practice whose future depends on responsible design choices that balance capability, safety, and human oversight.
